# Testament of Issachar — 5
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

If Reuben confessed lust and Simeon confessed jealousy and Judah confessed wine and women — Issachar has almost nothing to confess. His testament is quieter than the others. It's the testimony of a man who simply lived well.

**1** I am Issachar, fifth son of Jacob. I was born as the price of mandrakes.

**2** Here's the story: Reuben brought mandrakes home from the field. Rachel saw them and wanted them. Leah and Rachel struck a deal — Rachel got the mandrakes, Leah got Jacob for a night. Jacob lay with Leah. She conceived. She named me Issachar: the wage, the reward.

**3** An angel appeared to Leah afterward and told her she would have two more children, because she had given her husband to her sister out of modesty rather than spite. And Rachel too would eventually bear children — not from pleasure-seeking, but from her genuine longing for a child. That's how Joseph and Benjamin came.

**4** I grew up a simple man. I farmed. I brought my father the produce of the field each season. I didn't pry into other people's business. I didn't envy anyone. I didn't scheme. I walked in uprightness and my father blessed me for it.

**5** I never had double-dealing in my heart. I never carried hatred toward anyone. I was single-minded — before God and before people.

**6** I loved God with everything I had, and I loved every person the way I love my children.

**7** Sons, do the same. When you live in simplicity, the spirits of Beliar have nothing to grip. No wicked deed will get traction on you. Even the wild creation will yield to you — because you walk with God in an undivided heart.

**8** Guard simplicity. Walk in singleness. Don't stick your nose into your neighbor's affairs. Love God. Love your neighbor. Give to the poor and the weak.

**9** Work the earth. Bring firstfruits to God. He will bless the work of your hands, as he blessed every faithful worker from Abel to this day. The land is your inheritance. Tend it with gratitude.

**10** I know what will happen in the last days: my sons' sons will abandon simplicity. They will chase after greed. They will leave the farm and follow their own devices. They will be scattered. They will serve their enemies. Tell your children this — so that when they fall, they will know quickly where to return to. God is merciful. He will bring them back.

**11** I am 126 years old. And I can say this: I have known no woman but my wife. I have not fornicated, not even in my thoughts. I have not drunk wine to be led astray. I have not coveted anything that belonged to my neighbor. I have not told a single lie.

**12** When anyone was in distress, I felt it with them. I shared my bread with the hungry. I worked godliness and truth every day of my life.

**13** Do this, sons. The spirit of Beliar will leave you alone.

**14** After he said these things, he told his sons to carry him to Hebron and bury him with his fathers. He stretched out his feet and fell asleep in peace.

---
*End of Testament of Issachar*
